reasoning_notes: Every terminal sigma2 fixes slot 0 as a free word, so the first Fox row is uniform for all n; this is a genuine induction rather than finite sampling.
The scalar factorization through Z[t,t^-1] follows from conjugacy of oriented meridians and commutativity; the eR argument also correctly excludes nonzero nonunital scalar homomorphisms.
Identity (5) is a left-ideal identity and therefore suffices for the stated two-sided ideal conclusion; no semisimplicity or module classification is needed.
An integral lift gives 1+2W; central nilpotence of 2 makes 2W nilpotent and the finite geometric-series inverse is valid even though the group algebra is noncommutative.
Reduction of a unital positive-size matrix model over a nonzero local ring stays unital on the residue field; quotient factorization is required only after reduction as stated.

The PDF expressly leaves other quotient kernels, odd characteristic, characteristic zero noncommuting models, other generating systems, and ordinary group rank unresolved; no converse rank inference is used.

determinant_argument_checks: The integer Fox images are fixed for all n because the relator and top permutation images are fixed.
S is in the image of the two-sided Fox ideal and S=1+2W follows from the assumed mod-two identity.
Right multiplication T_S on the rank-20160 free abelian group Z[A8] is an ordinary integer matrix; its reduction modulo two is I.
Its determinant d is therefore congruent to 1 modulo two and hence is odd and nonzero; no numerical determinant evaluation is needed.
The integral adjugate c=adj(T_S)(1) is an integer group-ring element; T_S(c)=cS=d*1. This multiplication direction agrees with the printed right-multiplication convention.
Because S belongs to the two-sided image ideal, cS=d*1 belongs to it.
A unital homomorphism to M_m(R), m>=1, that kills the ideal sends d*1 to d*I_m=0, giving d*1_R=0.
For nonzero R this forces positive characteristic dividing |d|; since d is odd there are only finitely many possible odd characteristics. No existence of models in those characteristics follows.
The proof does not establish d=+1 or -1, and the PDF explicitly says so.
The remaining-scope paragraph correctly leaves odd exceptional characteristics for this quotient and characteristic-zero models through other quotients unresolved.
